result.stdout:
Usage: hcat [options] [[serve|inspect|pipe] [dir] [-- command...]]

Instant HTTP server: serve a folder, catch incoming requests, or pipe a command over HTTP.

Options:
  --lan                        Bind 0.0.0.0 to share on the local network (prints a QR code).
  --local                      Force loopback-only binding (overrides --lan/--host).
  --https                      Enable TLS with an in-memory self-signed certificate.
  --upload                     (serve) Enable the POST upload receiver.
  --spa                        (serve) SPA fallback: unmatched browser navigations return the index file.
  --spa-index FILE             (serve, with --spa) SPA fallback filename (default index.html).
  --host ADDR                  Explicit bind address.
  --port N                     Listen port (default 8080).
  --upload-dir DIR             (serve) Upload target directory (default ./uploads).
  --status CODE                (inspect) HTTP status to respond with (default 200).
  --capture N                  (CI) Exit after capturing N requests.
  --exit-on EXPR               (CI) Exit when a request matches: path=/x, method=POST, body~text (body~ is inspect-only).
  --timeout DUR                (CI) Fail if the stop condition is not met within DUR (e.g. 30s, 5m).
  -h, --help                   Show help
  --version                    Show version
  --no-color                   Disable colored output
  --json                       JSON output
  --describe                   Structured JSON metadata for AI agents
  --color[=auto|always|never]  Coloured output: auto (default when omitted), always, or never

Examples:
  hcat                       Serve the current directory (localhost)
  hcat serve ./public --lan  Share a folder on your LAN (QR printed)
  hcat inspect --lan         Catch and print incoming webhooks
  hcat pipe -- jq .          Expose jq over HTTP

Exit Codes:
  0    Success (clean shutdown, or a CI stop condition was met)
  1    A CI stop condition (--capture/--exit-on) was not met before --timeout elapsed
[truncated]
